fatal_errors: The proposed initial material is an as-cast bulk alloy, whereas the reconstructed HEBM route starts from high-purity elemental powders; no comminution or powder-production step is specified to make the stated starting state compatible with ball milling.

The cast baseline is described as homogeneous and predominantly FCC, while the target comparison emphasizes porosity and microstructural heterogeneity; this weakens the claimed causal attribution to coarse FCC grains alone.
explanation: The hypothesis closely reconstructs the processing window, nanocrystalline FCC/BCC mediator, Hall-Petch and dislocation-based strengthening, and the principal hardness and compressive-strength outcomes. It also supplies appropriate hardness, compression, and XRD measurements. However, it conflates the low-strength cast comparison with the actual elemental-powder feedstock for HEBM and overstates the cast alloy as homogeneous and nearly pure FCC. The experiment compares two highly different routes, simultaneously changing porosity, grain size, dislocation density, and phase fraction, so it can demonstrate improvement but cannot cleanly determine which mechanism governs it. Stronger discrimination would require matched-density controls, milling-time and SPS-temperature series, and independent grain-size or phase-fraction controls. The predicted density, yield stress, and intergranular fracture behavior are also omitted. With no cited evidence and several exact numerical claims, evidence discipline is only moderate.
